image_description: A grand, ornate pipe organ situated on a balcony within a Gothic-style cathedral. The organ features multiple tiers of vertical metallic pipes of varying heights, arranged in symmetrical clusters with decorative wooden casework. The background shows intricate stone vaulted ceilings and arches. A decorative railing runs along the front of the organ loft.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The stone texture of the ceiling ribs appears slightly smudged or painterly compared to the sharper details of the organ pipes, suggesting minor generative smoothing or resolution loss in the background.
The decorative railing in the foreground has inconsistent spacing and geometry. Some vertical bars seem to merge into the horizontal rail or fade out irregularly, lacking precise mechanical logic.
The curvature of the leftmost pipe group seems slightly exaggerated or warped relative to the straight lines of the architecture, though this could also be a wide-angle lens effect.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific classification of the instrument as a pipe organ and distinguish it from other architectural structures.
To verify the spatial relationship between the foreground organ, the mid-ground railing, and the background vaulted ceiling, ensuring no melting occurs.
To check for fusion between individual pipes and the wooden casing, ensuring each pipe is a distinct, closed object.
To assess overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect subtle textural artifacts in the stone and wood materials.

focus_areas: Boundary integrity between individual metal pipes
Geometric consistency of the decorative railing

Symmetry and alignment of pipe clusters
